contract: One paid order leads to exactly one fulfillment, even when the webhook is delivered more than once, concurrently, or under a different event ID; a failed fulfillment is never marked complete.

attempts.diagnosis: The handler does a check-then-await-then-record sequence. It reads the order status, awaits several times, and only sets 'fulfilled' after fulfillOrder resolves. Overlapping deliveries therefore all see a non-fulfilled order and each call fulfillOrder. The same race lets different event IDs for one order fulfill it twice.
attempts.changeSummary: Added a per-order in-flight promise map. The check for a fulfilled order and the registration of the in-flight fulfillment happen synchronously, with no await between them. Overlapping deliveries wait for the in-flight attempt. If it succeeded they return 'duplicate'. If it failed they loop and one of them becomes the next single attempt, so fulfillment is never concurrent. The order is marked 'fulfilled' only after fulfillOrder succeeds. A failure is rethrown to the delivery that ran it, and the in-flight entry is cleared so a retry can fulfill exactly once. The order lookup is now synchronous so it cannot interleave.

details.summary: Probes check-then-await-then-record races and per-order idempotency in the webhook handler. The tests cover sequential duplicates, concurrent deliveries of one event, concurrent deliveries under different event IDs for one order, unrelated orders, ignored event types, and a fulfillment failure followed by retry (including the failure under concurrency). The original handler awaits before it sets any in-flight marker and only sets 'fulfilled' after fulfillment, so concurrent deliveries should each call fulfillOrder.

generatedTests.summary: Probes check-then-await-then-record races and per-order idempotency in the webhook handler. The tests cover sequential duplicates, concurrent deliveries of one event, concurrent deliveries under different event IDs for one order, unrelated orders, ignored event types, and a fulfillment failure followed by retry (including the failure under concurrency). The original handler awaits before it sets any in-flight marker and only sets 'fulfilled' after fulfillment, so concurrent deliveries should each call fulfillOrder.
